operation_details.item: The user's North America business unit runs its ERP on SAP.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: For the upcoming board discussion, I suggest we frame the IT architecture review around the operating model rather than presenting a system-by-system inventory.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Agreed. The Europe business unit runs its ERP on Oracle.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That gives us a useful starting point. We can show where regional choices reflect local operating needs and where standardization may still be practical.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: The Asia business unit runs its ERP on NetSuite.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: The contrast between the regions will make the strategic trade-offs more visible. I would avoid implying that one platform must immediately replace the others.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: The North America business unit runs its ERP on SAP.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Understood. We can position the landscape as a portfolio decision, with integration, control, and execution risk considered alongside license economics.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: The IT architecture review covers all three units.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: For the review materials, I recommend a single comparison page followed by a short decision log. That should be concise enough for the board while preserving the operational detail needed by the team.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Please make the decision log explicit about integration dependencies and ownership, rather than presenting only a preferred end state.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: I will structure it around current platforms, critical dependencies, accountable owners, and the decisions that require executive direction.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: That approach will keep the board conversation focused on choices and consequences.
